Correction to the name-flag steer, Jack Heart: "but my question is --job NAMING or SELECTING te job" then "i think it should be selecting?". --job SELECTS a job the file defines in Python (training(train, config=..., name="wide", seeds=...)); jobs are named only in Python, never on the command line. No --job when the file defines one job or just train(config). --config overrides fields of the selected job's config (or the default config). --run names the one run being made, exactly as typed; refused with several seeds. A selected multi-seed job with no --run trains each seed here in turn as JOB-seed-N, like launch (operator's choice, not Jack's). Same meaning in launch/continue/eval. Words in scratch/demo-hanabi.md.
